stem:
Ira looks at the diagram. On the same flat page, lines $\ell$ and $m$ are each perpendicular to line $n$.

Which claim correctly decides how $\ell$ and $m$ relate?

options.text: $\ell$ is parallel to $m$, because both are perpendicular to the same line $n$ on the same flat page.
Call the answer the shared reference line $n$ itself.
Call $\ell$ and $m$ parallel even if they need not stay on the same flat page.
Treat the right-angle marks as also proving that $n$ is parallel to $\ell$.

teacher.key_rationale: In the same plane, two lines perpendicular to the same line are parallel. Naming n alone, dropping same-plane, or stretching the marks to claim n parallel to l miss that test.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source triangle rods as coplanar lines l and m both perpendicular to reference line n.
